description: PART C — Replace the chef + trainer Web Speech voices with playback of the recorded MP3s. Rewrite lib/chef/chefVoice.ts to play public/audio/chef-voice.mp3 and lib/coach/coachVoice.ts to play public/audio/personal-trainer.mp3 over an HTMLAudioElement, wiring a Web Audio AnalyserNode so getLoudness() returns REAL amplitude (a genuine improvement over the old sine fallback). PRESERVE the exact interface the scenes/chatbots depend on: speak(text,{onStart,onEnd}), setMuted, getLoudness, dispose; anti-overlap; static-export safe; play only from the user's send gesture. Depends on FEAT-001. Independent of FEAT-002/FEAT-003 (touches only lib voice files), so it may be implemented before or after them.
steps: Rewrite lib/chef/chefVoice.ts (class ChefVoice): keep the same public API — constructor, get isMuted, setMuted(muted), speak(text, {onStart,onEnd}), getLoudness(): number, dispose(). Replace the SpeechSynthesis internals with an HTMLAudioElement created lazily on the client (guard typeof window/Audio) whose src = asset('/audio/chef-voice.mp3'). Set crossOrigin='anonymous' is unnecessary (same-origin static file); set preload appropriately.

speak(): if muted, no-op (fire no callbacks). Otherwise STOP any currently-playing clip first (anti-overlap: pause + reset currentTime, detach handlers), then play the MP3. Fire onStart when playback actually begins (the 'playing' event or the play() promise resolving) and onEnd on the 'ended' event, on 'error', and on cancel/stop. The MP3 is a FIXED recording that does NOT match arbitrary reply text — so `text` is used only to decide whether to play (non-empty) / for logging, NOT synthesized. This is the user's explicit instruction; the speaking window is driven by the real audio duration.

Wire real loudness: lazily create a Web Audio AudioContext + MediaElementAudioSourceNode(audioEl) + AnalyserNode (connect source -> analyser -> destination so audio still plays). getLoudness() reads the analyser's time-domain (or frequency) data and returns a smoothed 0..1 RMS. Return 0 when not playing or muted. Resume the AudioContext inside the user-gesture speak() call (autoplay policy). Guard for browsers without AudioContext — fall back to getLoudness()->0 (scene then uses its sine fallback) and still play the audio.

setMuted(true) must stop/mute playback immediately and close the speaking window; setMuted(false) restores. dispose() must stop playback, disconnect the audio graph, close the AudioContext, remove listeners, and release the element. Handle the browser autoplay policy: since speak() is only ever called from the send gesture (see ChefChatbot/CoachChatbot), play() is allowed; still catch the play() promise rejection and route it through onEnd so a blocked play never wedges the speaking window.

Apply the SAME rewrite to lib/coach/coachVoice.ts (class CoachVoice) using asset('/audio/personal-trainer.mp3'). Keep its identical public API. getLoudness now real, so the coach's whole-group/limb motion can track amplitude (CoachScene already prefers loudness over the sine fallback).

Update the module doc comments in both files to describe the new MP3-playback + AnalyserNode approach and DROP the stale 'no audio file / Web Speech' license text. Do NOT change ChefChatbot.tsx / CoachChatbot.tsx call sites unless a signature detail requires it — the interface is preserved. Confirm both chatbots still pass getLoudness to their scenes and call speak/onStart/onEnd/setMuted/dispose unchanged.

SURFACE the tradeoff clearly in the findings: because the MP3 is a fixed recording, the voice plays the SAME recorded line regardless of the reply text shown; 'speaks the actual words' becomes 'plays the recorded voice line while the reply is displayed'. This is the user's explicit instruction.
Verify lint + build, then commit on the branch (do NOT push).
acceptance_criteria: lib/chef/chefVoice.ts and lib/coach/coachVoice.ts play their respective MP3s via HTMLAudioElement and keep the exact public API (speak/{onStart,onEnd}, setMuted, getLoudness, dispose).
getLoudness() returns a real 0..1 amplitude from a Web Audio AnalyserNode while playing (0 when idle/muted), with a graceful 0 fallback when AudioContext is unavailable.
Anti-overlap: starting a new clip stops the previous one; onStart fires on real playback start, onEnd fires on ended/error/cancel.
setMuted stops/mutes immediately; dispose tears down the audio graph and listeners; all client-side and static-export safe (no SSR crash).
ChefChatbot/CoachChatbot compile against the unchanged interface; npm run lint (font warning only) and npm run build both pass.
The fixed-recording-vs-reply-text tradeoff is documented in the feature findings.
verification: export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH && npm run lint && npm run build
grep -n 'speak\|getLoudness\|setMuted\|dispose' components/chef/ChefChatbot.tsx components/coach/CoachChatbot.tsx  (confirm call sites unchanged)
findings:
Rewrote lib/chef/chefVoice.ts (ChefVoice) and lib/coach/coachVoice.ts (CoachVoice) to replace the Web Speech API with playback of the recorded MP3s via a lazily-created HTMLAudioElement: asset('/audio/chef-voice.mp3') for the chef, asset('/audio/personal-trainer.mp3') for the coach. The exact public interface is preserved (constructor, get isMuted, setMuted, speak(text,{onStart,onEnd}), getLoudness, dispose) so ChefChatbot.tsx / CoachChatbot.tsx call sites were NOT touched and still compile.

FIXED-RECORDING-VS-REPLY-TEXT TRADEOFF (user's explicit instruction): the MP3 is a single fixed recording, so speak(text) does NOT synthesize the reply words — it plays the SAME recorded voice line every time. `text` is used ONLY to decide whether to play (a non-empty reply opens the speaking window) and is never spoken. The speaking window is driven by the REAL audio duration (onStart on the 'playing' event, onEnd on 'ended'/'error'/cancel/stop). So the previous 'speaks the actual reply words' behavior becomes 'plays the recorded voice line while the reply text is displayed'. This is a deliberate consequence of using recorded MP3s rather than TTS.

getLoudness() is now a genuine improvement: a Web Audio graph (AudioContext -> MediaElementAudioSourceNode(audioEl) -> AnalyserNode -> destination) yields a real smoothed 0..1 RMS amplitude while the clip plays, so the chef's jaw and the coach's motion track the actual voice (both scenes already prefer loudness over their sine fallback). getLoudness() returns 0 when idle/muted; if AudioContext is unavailable it falls back to 0 while still playing the audio. The AudioContext is resumed inside the user-gesture speak() call to satisfy autoplay policy, and the play() promise rejection is caught and routed through onEnd so a blocked autoplay never wedges the speaking window. Anti-overlap: a new clip stops the previous one first. setMuted(true) stops playback immediately and closes the window; dispose() stops playback, disconnects the graph, closes the AudioContext, and releases the element. All lazy/client-side (guarded by typeof window / typeof Audio) so no SSR/static-export crash.

No dependencies added (HTMLAudioElement + Web Audio API are browser built-ins). WS3 (engine/state routing) untouched — only the audio source changed.

BUILD NOTE: the current TS lib.dom types require Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> (not the default ArrayBufferLike) for AnalyserNode.getByteTimeDomainData; declared the analyser buffer as Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> and constructed it via new Uint8Array(new ArrayBuffer(fftSize)) to satisfy the type checker.

VERIFIED: `npm run lint` -> only the expected @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning in app/layout.tsx (0 errors). `npm run build` -> static export succeeds, all 7 routes prerender. Confirmed ChefChatbot.tsx/CoachChatbot.tsx still pass getLoudness to their scenes and call speak/onStart/onEnd/setMuted/dispose unchanged.
